newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch set rotation scheme for ABN options trade.
newsitem.headline: Dutch set rotation scheme for ABN options trade.

text.p: Amsterdam Exchanges said that it had been forced to suspend the continuous free trade in ABN AMRO options on Wednesday in favour of a rotation system due to the massive flood of orders.
ABN AMRO options prices on Wednesday were determined according to the 'rotation' system customarily only used to set opening prices, the bourse said in a statement.

Under the rotation system, all orders received by floor brokers in the various series are first collated and then market makers are invited to submit bid and offer quotes after which an opening price is set.

The flood of ABN AMRO orders meant this system had to be maintained throughout the day, with a last rotation still in the process of being implemented at 1505 GMT, more than half an hour after close of stock exchange trade.
Amsterdam Exchanges said that in the interim, measures had been implemented to ensure speedy order processing, stressing Wednesday's flood of orders had been exceptional.
At 3.2 million contracts, trade in options on ABN AMRO outstripped that of any other European stock option during the first half of this year.
